items.title: Court Bars Meta From Using News Articles to Train AI in Brazil
items.excerpt: A São Paulo court on Nov. 3 barred Meta from using bots to collect news articles, photos and videos from outlets in three Brazilian press associations to train AI; daily fines could reach $182,400.
items.rationale: Primary decision (court injunction, Nov. 3) on AI training and copyright with concrete fines; policy/litigation axis, separate case from the EU advocate-general opinion published 11-04.

items.title: Voters deliver "AI earthquake," rebuking tech and billionaires
items.excerpt: Voters approved dozens of data center moratoriums; per Ballotpedia about two dozen of 41 restrict/block measures across 10 states appeared to pass, and Texas governor-elect Hinojosa campaigned on keeping a data center construction moratorium until the legislature acts.
items.rationale: Single card for the 5-outlet midterm data-center cluster; chosen for its concrete ballot-measure count (Ballotpedia: ~24 of 41 restrict/block measures in 10 states). Writer must frame it as measures passed, not as partisan win/loss or poll commentary, and must not use the 'AI earthquake' framing as fact.

items.title: Metsola tells MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws
items.excerpt: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola told MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws, as the Parliament prepares guidelines for lawmakers on the use of AI.
items.rationale: Institutional instruction from the European Parliament President plus forthcoming internal AI-use guidelines for lawmakers; new rule-setting on AI in the legislative process.

items.title: EU rules on Artificial Intelligence devices will apply in NI
items.excerpt: The UK government says some EU AI rules, covering AI-integrated products, will apply in Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework.
items.rationale: UK government decision that parts of the EU AI Act (AI-integrated products) apply in Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework; a concrete compliance change for product builders, a cross-border regulatory split.

items.title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
items.excerpt: The AI minister now concedes the estimated figure is less than a third of that. Researchers blame the country’s slow rate of adoption.
items.rationale: National AI strategy: the UK AI minister revises the official headline estimate to under a third of £400B, and the figure's origin in Google-commissioned research. Attribute the sourcing claim to WIRED and the revision to the minister.
